modules.title: Portfolio and capstones
modules.summary: Apply your skills to three realistic documentation assignments.

lessons.title: What API documentation is
lessons.summary: Learn to explain an API as a useful product, not merely a list of URLs.
objectives: Identify the reader and their task
Distinguish an API contract from a working integration
Define a useful documentation outcome

lessons.title: Choose the right documentation type
lessons.summary: Separate learning, task instructions, explanations, and lookup reference so readers can find the right level of help.
objectives: Choose a format for a developer question
Plan a quickstart that produces an observable result
Connect tutorials and reference pages without duplicating them

lessons.title: Writing style and information architecture
lessons.summary: Write descriptions that explain behavior, constraints, and decisions instead of repeating a field name.
objectives: Rewrite vague API prose
Use consistent names and task-based headings
Organize a page for scanning and accessibility

lessons.title: Gather information and interview engineers
lessons.summary: Build an evidence-based documentation plan from tickets, schemas, implementation, and reproducible tests.
objectives: Create a documentation evidence map
Ask targeted SME questions
Separate confirmed behavior from assumptions

lessons.title: HTTP requests, URLs, and responses
lessons.summary: Learn to read the request and response envelope before interpreting the business data.
objectives: Identify the parts of an HTTP request
Distinguish path parameters from query parameters
Explain content negotiation and HTTPS

lessons.title: JSON, YAML, and schema fundamentals
lessons.summary: Distinguish valid syntax from a valid API request, and learn to describe nested data accurately.
objectives: Read nested objects and arrays
Explain missing, null, empty, and default values
Use schemas to describe structure and constraints

lessons.title: Test APIs with cURL, Postman, and browser tools
lessons.summary: Capture reproducible evidence and learn what each tool can and cannot establish.
objectives: Run and inspect a REST request
Use environment variables without exposing secrets
Record success and failure evidence for documentation

lessons.title: JavaScript fetch for technical writers
lessons.summary: Write examples that handle network problems, HTTP errors, and empty bodies without hiding what happened.
objectives: Read async JavaScript request code
Handle HTTP failures separately from rejected promises
Explain timeouts and browser CORS behavior

lessons.title: Resources and REST principles
lessons.summary: Understand the design ideas behind an HTTP API without assuming that every JSON endpoint is fully RESTful.
objectives: Model resources and representations
Explain stateless requests
Distinguish REST constraints from common URL conventions

lessons.title: Methods, safety, and idempotency
lessons.summary: Explain GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS without reducing them to misleading CRUD labels.
objectives: Distinguish safe from idempotent methods
Explain replacement versus partial update
Document repeat-request behavior accurately

lessons.title: Parameters, filtering, sorting, and pagination
lessons.summary: Make collection documentation precise enough to support reliable iteration, not just the first page.
objectives: Document parameter location and serialization
Compare offset and cursor pagination
Explain sort order, limits, and changing datasets

lessons.title: Status codes and Problem Details
lessons.summary: Write error documentation that explains what happened and what the developer should do next.
objectives: Interpret success and error statuses in context
Read an RFC 9457-style error representation
Distinguish retryable conditions from input and state problems

lessons.title: Anatomy of a complete endpoint reference
lessons.summary: Build a reference page that answers the questions a developer asks immediately before and after a request.
objectives: Create a predictable endpoint-page structure
Document fields and side effects together
Provide complete success and failure examples

lessons.title: Product API documentation workshop
lessons.summary: Apply the reference structure to reads, creation, replacement, partial update, and deletion.
objectives: Compare six product operations
Write accurate money and markdown descriptions
Explain ownership and write constraints

lessons.title: Write a cart-to-order integration guide
lessons.summary: Document a multi-step purchase workflow, including transferred IDs, state changes, and recovery.
objectives: Create a sequence with explicit prerequisites
Explain order snapshotting and cart closure
Handle uncertain order-creation outcomes

lessons.title: Troubleshooting and trustworthy code samples
lessons.summary: Build diagnostic guidance that narrows a problem instead of asking readers to try random fixes.
objectives: Write symptom-cause-check-fix guidance
Audit sample code for hidden assumptions
Separate API defects from expected validation failures

lessons.title: Authentication, authorization, and OAuth
lessons.summary: Explain how callers obtain access and what they are permitted to do without confusing tokens, identities, and scopes.
objectives: Distinguish authentication from authorization
Explain common OAuth use cases
Document the demo tokens without presenting them as production security

lessons.title: Rate limits, retries, and idempotency keys
lessons.summary: Give developers a recovery policy that avoids unnecessary traffic and accidental duplicate work.
objectives: Explain uncertain outcomes and retry conditions
Document idempotency scope and retention
Distinguish a rate-limit simulation from real quota enforcement

lessons.title: Caching, API evolution, and deprecation
lessons.summary: Document representation freshness and change management without promising compatibility that the API cannot guarantee.
objectives: Explain ETags and conditional requests
Separate API versions from specification versions
Assess additive and breaking changes

lessons.title: Webhooks, asynchronous work, and uploads
lessons.summary: Document event-driven integrations and long-running tasks while keeping unimplemented examples clearly labelled.
objectives: Describe webhook delivery and verification
Explain polling for asynchronous operations
Document multipart upload requirements

lessons.title: OpenAPI, Swagger, and version numbers
lessons.summary: Learn what an OpenAPI description does and choose a supported baseline without confusing it with the API itself.
objectives: Distinguish the specification from tooling
Read the top-level OpenAPI structure
Explain three independent version numbers

lessons.title: Document OpenAPI operations
lessons.summary: Describe methods, inputs, responses, and headers with correct requiredness and clear operation identities.
objectives: Build a Path Item and Operation Object
Separate request-body presence from property presence
Describe response bodies and relevant headers

lessons.title: Reusable models, constraints, and examples
lessons.summary: Build a coherent schema library without losing the differences between input and output representations.
objectives: Use components and references correctly
Model nested objects and constrained values
Separate reusable structure from operation-specific behavior

lessons.title: Security schemes and complete API descriptions
lessons.summary: Describe public and protected operations accurately, including alternatives, combined requirements, and the limits of contract declarations.
objectives: Define bearer and illustrative OAuth schemes
Apply security globally or per operation
Understand OR and AND semantics in security requirements

lessons.title: Advanced schemas: composition and nullability
lessons.summary: Model alternative shapes and shared constraints without assuming that schema composition behaves like object-oriented inheritance.
objectives: Compare oneOf, anyOf, and allOf
Express nullable values in OpenAPI 3.1
Identify common closed-object composition traps

lessons.title: Links, callbacks, webhooks, and multipart descriptions
lessons.summary: Describe advanced HTTP relationships without falsely advertising features that the server does not implement.
objectives: Distinguish links, callbacks, and webhooks
Represent multipart request bodies
Keep illustrative contracts separate from the live API

lessons.title: Authoring, bundling, and publishing an OpenAPI description
lessons.summary: Choose a source-of-truth workflow that prevents generated files and hand-written guidance from drifting apart.
objectives: Compare design-first and code-first workflows
Explain references and bundling
Plan a reproducible publication pipeline

lessons.title: Validate contracts and prevent documentation drift
lessons.summary: Design checks that distinguish syntactic correctness, schema correctness, runtime agreement, and editorial quality.
objectives: Build a layered validation strategy
Test examples against schemas
Report validation coverage honestly

lessons.title: GraphQL and REST: choose by the problem
lessons.summary: Understand the two interface styles using the same marketplace task rather than treating them as competing slogans.
objectives: Explain the GraphQL execution model at a high level
Compare request and response shapes
Discuss tradeoffs without unsupported performance claims

lessons.title: Read GraphQL SDL and nullability
lessons.summary: Translate type signatures into precise documentation about objects, inputs, lists, and values.
objectives: Read object, input, scalar, and enum definitions
Interpret list and non-null wrappers
Distinguish input presence from output selection

lessons.title: Queries, variables, aliases, and fragments
lessons.summary: Write reusable GraphQL operations and explain how their selections determine the response shape.
objectives: Build a named query with variables
Use aliases and fragments correctly
Predict nested response keys

lessons.title: Mutations, inputs, payloads, and side effects
lessons.summary: Document GraphQL writes as business operations with explicit validation, state changes, and result handling.
objectives: Read a mutation input and payload
Explain serial root-field execution without implying transactions
Document business failures in the implemented error model

lessons.title: Validation, coercion, nullability, and errors
lessons.summary: Learn to explain failures without hiding successful fields or confusing missing values with null.
objectives: Distinguish request failures from execution failures
Explain null propagation using the schema
Document partial responses and stable error codes

lessons.title: GraphQL pagination and collection contracts
lessons.summary: Document forward pagination without treating a popular connection pattern as part of every GraphQL API.
objectives: Read edges, nodes, cursors, and pageInfo
Write a correct next-page workflow
Explain limits and cursor stability

lessons.title: Interfaces, unions, directives, and introspection
lessons.summary: Learn the schema features writers encounter while keeping illustrative extensions separate from the live marketplace.
objectives: Explain interfaces and unions
Use __typename and inline fragments
Describe directives, introspection, and deprecation

lessons.title: GraphQL transport and operational concerns
lessons.summary: Separate the GraphQL language from HTTP behavior, runtime limits, subscriptions, and platform-specific architecture.
objectives: Describe a complete GraphQL HTTP request
Explain operational risks without universal claims
Identify extension features that the demo does not implement

lessons.title: Document a GraphQL schema beyond its field names
lessons.summary: Turn SDL into a useful business reference with constraints, relationships, and precise value semantics.
objectives: Write descriptions that add information
Build complete field and argument tables
Document scalar and relationship behavior

lessons.title: GraphQL query reference workshop
lessons.summary: Write operation pages that a developer can execute and adapt without reconstructing missing context.
objectives: Build a complete query reference
Provide matching variables and response selections
Cover missing data and permissions

lessons.title: GraphQL mutation reference workshop
lessons.summary: Document writes as state transitions with validation, permissions, and recovery guidance.
objectives: Describe mutation preconditions and side effects
Write complete input and payload examples
Explain safe recovery from uncertain outcomes

lessons.title: Write a GraphQL purchase-flow guide
lessons.summary: Connect individual operations into a reproducible integration without hiding state or promising unrealistic transaction behavior.
objectives: Plan a multi-step GraphQL tutorial
Carry identifiers and retry keys across steps
Compare REST and GraphQL fairly

lessons.title: Docs-as-code: Markdown, Git, and review
lessons.summary: Treat documentation changes as reviewable, versioned product work rather than untracked files.
objectives: Use a simple documentation branch workflow
Separate source content from generated output
Write a useful documentation pull request

lessons.title: Test documentation at several layers
lessons.summary: Build a quality plan that catches broken examples, misleading contracts, and unusable pages.
objectives: Distinguish content, contract, runtime, and browser checks
Design representative positive and negative tests
Report results honestly

lessons.title: Release notes, deprecation, and migration guides
lessons.summary: Explain API changes in terms of consumer impact, required action, and verified compatibility.
objectives: Classify additive and breaking changes carefully
Write actionable release notes
Create before-and-after migration guidance

lessons.title: Work with engineering teams and release owners
lessons.summary: Build a documentation workflow with clear questions, ownership, and release-readiness evidence.
objectives: Run focused SME reviews
Define documentation acceptance criteria
Use metrics without confusing activity with quality

lessons.title: Capstone: build a REST documentation package
lessons.summary: Use the course tools to produce a complete, testable developer documentation set.
objectives: Plan a coherent REST documentation deliverable
Validate references against the implementation
Assess the result with a weighted rubric

lessons.title: Capstone: build a GraphQL documentation package
lessons.summary: Create a field-aware developer guide that explains both schema structure and real integration behavior.
objectives: Combine schema and operation references
Document a working GraphQL workflow
Assess nullability, errors, and pagination explanations

lessons.title: Capstone: maintain documentation through an API change
lessons.summary: Practice impact analysis across contracts, examples, release notes, and migration guidance.
objectives: Analyze a realistic multi-part change request
Update all affected documentation artifacts
Separate confirmed decisions from draft assumptions

lessons.title: Assemble and review your API-writing portfolio
lessons.summary: Present your work as an honest, coherent demonstration of technical writing skills.
objectives: Package a portfolio around reader outcomes
Explain evidence and limitations
Plan useful next improvements
